cards.title: Supporting Your Pregnant Friend With Babies
cards.body: You likely underestimate your ability to connect with your friend's baby since you haven't met them yet. Everyone relates to infants differently, so don't assume you'll be uncomfortable until you actually spend time together.

cards.title: Should You Move Closer to Family Before School?
cards.body: Moving back home for family support is tempting, but it comes with hidden costs beyond finances. Give new friendships time to develop before making a major relocation decision.

cards.title: Adult Children Moving Back Home: What to Expect
cards.body: When graduates return home due to economic pressures, parents must adjust their caregiving expectations. The transition from holiday visits to extended cohabitation requires new boundaries and communication.

cards.title: Postpartum Anxiety: A Practical Coping Cheat Sheet
cards.body: New mothers can manage postpartum anxiety more effectively with bite-sized, actionable advice. Quick reference tools help busy parents implement coping strategies during overwhelming moments.

cards.title: Quieting Food Noise in Children
cards.body: If your child seems obsessed with food or constantly thinks about eating, changing your feeding approach can help. Reducing "food noise" involves adjusting how families talk about and offer food.

cards.title: Reconciling With Estranged Children: Listen First
cards.body: Many estranged parents fear acknowledging their child's pain, but understanding their perspective is crucial for healing. Active listening often becomes the breakthrough moment in family reconciliation.

cards.title: Junior Doctor Burnout Threatens Maternity Care
cards.body: Trainee doctors delivering babies experience higher burnout rates than other specialties, putting patient safety at risk. Overworked maternity staff need better support to maintain quality care for families.
